title: Legacy fast endpoints share the same URL name
reasoning: Both the user-scoped legacy endpoint and the no-user endpoint are registered with name="fast_on_date". Any code that uses Django URL reversing by name cannot explicitly target the /hub/fast/ route; generated links, schema output, or redirects may resolve to the sibling legacy route instead of the intended no-user route depending on resolver behavior and ordering. The associated fast view tests import and exercise FastListView and FastByFeastDateView, but do not cover FastOnDateWithoutUser or reverse() behavior for this route name collision.
recommendation: Give the FastOnDateWithoutUser route a distinct name, such as fast_on_date_without_user or legacy_fast_on_date_public, and update any callers that reverse the no-user endpoint by name.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included fast tests focus on list, feast-date lookup, and serializer day numbering behavior; they do not assert route names, URL reversing, or request handling for the legacy /fast/ endpoint.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a URLconf test that reverse() can independently resolve both legacy endpoints by distinct names and that the no-user name resolves to /hub/fast/ under the mounted prefix.
minimumFixScope: Change the route name for path("fast/", FastOnDateWithoutUser.as_view(), ...) and update references to that URL name.
